BMultipoleParams:
BMultipoleParams

Defines magnetic (B) multipoles for an element. 

A given multipole can be set using any of the following:
- `KnX`: Order X normal strength in [1/m^(X+1)] (normalized, nonintegrated)
- `KsX`: Order X skew strength   in [1/m^(X+1)] (normalized, nonintegrated)
- `BnX`: Order X normal strength in [T/m^X] (unnormalized, nonintegrated)
- `BsX`: Order X skew strength   in [T/m^X] (unnormalized, nonintegrated)
- `KnXL`: Order X normal strength in [1/m^X] (normalized, integrated)
- `KsXL`: Order X skew strength in [1/m^X] (normalized, integrated)
- `BnXL`: Order X normal strength in [T/m^(X-1)] (unnormalized, integrated)
- `BsXL`: Order X skew strength in [T/m^(X-1)] (unnormalized, integrated)
- `tiltX`: Tilt to only order X multipole


The solenoidal multipole can be set using any of the above with `X` = `sol` and 
omitting the `n`/`s`, e.g. `Ksol`, `Bsol`, `KsolL`, `BsolL`.

!!! note
    The last *set* for a given multipole defines if both the normal and skew strengths 
    for a given multipole order are normalized and integrated. E.g.
    ```julia
    ele = LatElement(Kn1=0.1, Ks1=0.2, L=0.4) # Order 1 is normalized, nonintegrated
    ele.Kn1L = 0.3         # Order 1 independent variables are now normalized, integrated
    ele.Ks1L == 0.2*0.4    # true
    ele.Bn1 = 0.5          # Order 1 independent variables are now unnormalized, nonintegrated
    ele.Bs1 == 0.2*0.5/0.3 # true, set so that (Bs1/Bn1)_new = (Ks1L/Kn1L)_old
    ```
Beamline:
Beamline(line; kwargs...)

Constructs a `Beamline` out of the `LatElement`s in the vector `line`. The `LatElement`s 
in the `Beamline` will be automatically constructed as children of those `LatElement`s in 
`line`, inheriting all of their properties. 

The reference energy of the beamline may be optionally specified using one of the keyword 
arguments: `E_ref`, `pc_ref`, `p_over_q_ref`, `dE_ref`, `dpc_ref`, or `dp_over_q_ref`.
Whichever of these is specified will be the independent variable. The species of 
the beamline may be optionally specified using the `species_ref` keyword argument.
Specifying either of these keyword arguments will permanently override both the reference 
species and energy defined in the first `LatElement` -- see the warning below.

## Examples
```julia
qf = Quadrupole(Kn1=0.36, L=0.5)
d = Drift(L=1)
qd = Quadrupole(Kn1=-0.36, L=0.5)

fodo = Beamline([qf, d, qd, d], species_ref=Species("electron"), E_ref=18e9)
```

Alternatively, one can specify the reference species/energy in the first element:

```julia
qf = Quadrupole(Kn1=0.36, L=0.5, species_ref=Species("electron"), E_ref=18e9)
d = Drift(L=1)
qd = Quadrupole(Kn1=-0.36, L=0.5)

fodo = Beamline([qf, d, qd, d])
```

## Keyword arguments
- `context`: A `Context` struct containing variables that can be stored in the beamline
    for convenience. If the `Beamline` is put in a `Branch`, this is merged into the
    `Context` shared by the whole `Branch` -- see `Branch`.
- `species_ref`: Reference species of the beamline. 
- `E_ref`: Total reference energy [eV]
- `pc_ref`: Reference momentum [eV/c]
- `p_over_q_ref`: A *signed* reference magnetic rigidity [T * m]
- `dE_ref`: Change in total reference energy w.r.t. the directly-upstream beamline in 
    units [eV]
- `dpc_ref`: Change in reference momentum w.r.t. the directly-upstream beamline in 
    units [eV/c]
- `dp_over_q_ref`: Change in *signed* reference magnetic rigidty w.r.t. the directly 
    upstream beamline [T * m]

!!! warning
    Keyword arguments specified to the `Beamline` constructor will permanently override any 
    corresponding properties specified in the first `LatElement` of the beamline. E.g., 
    ```julia
    beg = Marker(species_ref=Species("electron"), E_ref=18e9)

    a = Beamline([beg])
    b = Beamline([beg], species_ref=Species("proton"), E_ref=1e9)

    a.E_ref == beg.E_ref == 18e9 # true
    b.E_ref == 1e9               # true
    b.E_ref != beg.E_ref         # true

    # If `beg` is reset:
    beg.species_ref = Species("positron")

    # `a` will still inherit it, but `b` will not:
    a.species_ref == beg.species_ref   # true
    b.species_ref == Species("proton") # true
    b.species_ref != beg.species_ref   # true
    ```
    Beamline

Structure containing a vector of `LatElement`s in an ordered sequence, and optionally 
a `Context` struct containing conrol variables associated with the beamline for 
convenience. The reference species (specified as `species_ref` and reference energy 
(specified as one of `E_ref`, `pc_ref`, `p_over_q_ref`, `dE_ref`, `dpc_ref`, or 
`dp_over_q_ref`) is uniform over the entire beamline. The most-recently specified of 
these reference energy quantites will be stored as the independent variable, in the 
first `LatElement` of the `Beamline`.

## Properties
- `line`: A read-only array of `LatElements` in the beamline, in order
- `context`: `Context` struct containing control variables associated with the beamline. If in a `Branch`, this is shared by the whole `Branch` (and `Lattice`, if any), and setting it sets it for all of them
- `branch`: `Branch` that the beamline is placed in, if any
- `branch_index`: Index of the beamline in the `Branch`, if in a `Branch`

Bunch:
Bunch(; v, state, spin, q, weight, callbacks, p_over_q_ref, t_ref, species)

Construct a `Bunch` of particles for tracking.

# Required Keyword Arguments
- `v::AbstractMatrix`: Matrix of particle phase space coordinates with shape 
  `(N, 6)`, where `N` is the number of particles and the 6 columns are the 
  canonical coordinates `[x px y py z pz]`.

# Optional Keyword Arguments
- `state`: Array of particle states with length `N`. Each element is a `UInt8` 
  flag indicating the particle status (e.g. `0x1 == STATE_ALIVE`). Defaults to all 
  particles alive.
- `spin::Bool=false`: If `true`, allocate identity quaternions for spin tracking.
- `q`: Matrix of spin quaternions with shape `(N, 4)`, where each row is a 
  unit quaternion `[q0 q1 q2 q3]`. Element type must match that of `v`.
- `weight`: Array of particle weights with length `N`, or `nothing` if 
   even weights for all particles. Defaults to `nothing`.
- `callbacks`: Tuple of functions to evaluate inside tracking kernels at each integration
  step (defaults to `()`), where each callback should be of the form 

```julia
callback(i, coords, p::TrackPoint)
``` 
  where `i` is the particle index, `coords` the `Coords` and `p` the point of the tracking (its s,
  reference time, step, ...; see `TrackPoint`).

- `p_over_q_ref`: Reference momentum-over-charge defining the normalization 
  of the phase space coordinates.
- `t_ref=0.`: Reference time.
- `species=Species()`: Particle species.

The `Bunch` also holds the position of its reference particle in the `Beamline`, `s` and `step` 
(as the callbacks get them). Tracking a `Beamline` starts them at 0, tracking a single element 
continues from them.

# Example
```julia
N = 1000
v = zeros(N, 6)
bunch = Bunch(v=v, species=Species("electron"), p_over_q_ref=-60.0)

# With spin tracking:
bunch = Bunch(v=v, spin=true, species=Species("electron"), p_over_q_ref=-60.0)
```
Context:
Context{T}

A "scope" of variables that can be used when evaluating `DefExpr`s. Contexts serve as a
single structure that stores all (control) variables associated with beamline parameters.
Contexts essentially act as structures with arbitrary field names. The type parameter `T`
can be specified as the variables' return type, or `Union` of return types, to improve
performance.

A `Beamline` stores a context, which is passed to all `DefExpr`s when getting parameters from
the `LatElement`s in it (a `Branch` or `Lattice` shares one context with all its `Beamline`s).
Elements that are not in a `Beamline` use `DEFAULT_CONTEXT`.

Values can be tried temporarily: `push!(c; name=value, ...)` sets the variables and remembers
their previous values, and `pop!(c)` restores them (a variable that `push!` added is removed
again). `withvalues(f, c; name=value, ...)` does the same around `f()`, also if it throws.

## Examples
```jldoctest
julia> qf = Quadrupole(Kn1=DefExpr(c -> c.k1), L=0.5);

julia> bl = Beamline([qf], context=Context(k1 = 0.36));

julia> bl.line[1].Kn1
0.36

julia> push!(bl.context; k1 = 0.4);

julia> bl.line[1].Kn1
0.4

julia> pop!(bl.context);

julia> bl.line[1].Kn1
0.36

julia> withvalues(bl.context; k1 = 0.5) do
         bl.line[1].Kn1
       end
0.5
```
DefExpr:
DefExpr{T}
  

A lazily-evaluated deferred expression returning type `T`. A deferred expression is a
function of a `Context` `c` that computes a value from the variables of the context, e.g.
`DefExpr(c -> -c.kq)`. It is evaluated every time the value is needed, with the current values
of the variables, so parameters that depend on each other never become "stale".

A parameter of an element in a `Beamline` is evaluated with the `Context` of the `Beamline`
(`bl.context`; a variable it does not have is taken from `DEFAULT_CONTEXT`). An element that is
not in a `Beamline` uses `DEFAULT_CONTEXT`.

Also see `Context`, `withvalues`, `rawget` and `deval`.

## Examples
```jldoctest
julia> qf = Quadrupole(L=0.5, Kn1=DefExpr(c -> c.kq));

julia> qd = Quadrupole(L=0.5, Kn1=DefExpr(c -> -c.kq));

julia> bl = Beamline([qf, Drift(L=1.0), qd], context=Context(kq=0.36));

julia> bl[qd].Kn1
-0.36

julia> bl.context.kq = 0.4;

julia> (bl[qf].Kn1, bl[qd].Kn1)
(0.4, -0.4)
```

Deferred expressions can be used in arithmetic like numbers: the result is a deferred
expression too. A deferred expression is evaluated in a `Context` by calling it with the
context, or with `deval`:
```jldoctest
julia> d = DefExpr(c -> c.a + c.b);

julia> c = Context(a=1.0, b=2.0);

julia> d(c)
3.0

julia> e = 2*d + 1;

julia> deval(e, c)
7.0
```

Knob:
Knob(obj, property; lower=-Inf, upper=Inf, step=Inf, name)
    Knob(obj, property, index; lower=-Inf, upper=Inf, step=Inf, name)
    Knob(get, set; lower=-Inf, upper=Inf, step=Inf, name="knob")
    @knob obj.property lower=... upper=...
    @knob obj.property[index] lower=... upper=...

Something that can be varied: the `property` of `obj` (a `LatElement`, a `Context`, a
`Controller`, or anything else with `obj.property` to get and set a number), or a pair of
functions `get()` and `set(value)`. `lower` and `upper` are the bounds used by `match!` and
`step` the largest change per iteration.

If the property is a vector of numbers (e.g. a variable of a `Context` holding the strengths of
several correctors), the knob stands for one knob per entry, named `property[1]`,
`property[2]`, ..., with the same bounds: `match!`, `value_and_jacobian` and `setknobs!` vary
each entry. `index` (or `@knob obj.property[index]`) is one entry alone.

A `Knob` is also a [`LatticeExpr`](@ref), so it can be used in expressions and targets.

Making a property a knob sets it, as `obj.property = value` does: if it was set to a deferred
expression, that dependence is replaced by the value.

## Examples
```julia
k1 = Knob(qf, :Kn1; lower=0, upper=1)
k2 = @knob ring.context.kqd
k3 = @knob ring.context.coilstrengths # one knob per entry of the vector
k4 = @knob ring.context.coilstrengths[2]
```

MapParams:
MapParams

Defines any arbitrary function to transport particle coordinates' and optionally spin 
quaternions. This could be a matrix, a neural network, a phase trombone, etc.

The input for the `transport_map` must be `(v, q, p=nothing)`, where `v` is a tuple of the
input phase space coordinates `(x, px, y, py, z, pz)` and `q` is `nothing` is there is no 
spin tracking, else `q` is a tuple of the input quaternion `(q0, q1, q2, q3)`. `p` may be a
tuple of parameters that can be used inside of the `transport_map`. This might be neural 
network weights, for example, or perhaps phase evolutions for a phase trombone.

For GPU compatibility, it is necessary that your function `transport_map` is GPU compatible:
there should be no type instabilities. You should also try to make your `transport_map` be
branchless, so both the CPU and GPU can vectorize it. 

`transport_map_params` should contain the tuple that is passed into `p` at the time of tracking.
## Properties:
- `transport_map`: Arbitrary function that transports particles' coordinates `v`, and optionally spin
  quaternions `q`.  Must have the signature `<your map name>(v, q, p=nothing)` and 
  returns the output as a tuple `(v, q)`
- `transport_map_params`: Parameters of the transport map that will be inputted as the `p` variable in `transport_map`


## Example
```julia
using StaticArrays
random_matrix = @SMatrix rand(6,6) # use StaticArrays for GPU compatibility

function matrix(v, q::Nothing, p) # `q::Nothing` -> no spin tracking
  # Vectorizable matrix multiplication by `p`:
  vx  = sum(p[1,:] .* v)
  vpx = sum(p[2,:] .* v)
  vy  = sum(p[3,:] .* v)
  vpy = sum(p[4,:] .* v)
  vz  = sum(p[5,:] .* v)
  vpz = sum(p[6,:] .* v)
  return ((vx, vpx, vy, vpy, vz, vpz), q)
end

m = LatElement(transport_map=matrix, transport_map_params=random_matrix)
```
MatchProblem:
MatchProblem(; vary, targets=[], minimize=[], minimize_weight=1)

A matching/optimization problem: the [`Knob`](@ref)s `vary` (or `obj => :property` pairs), the
[`Target`](@ref)s to meet, and expressions `minimize` whose sum of squares should be as small as
possible. [`match!`](@ref) solves it with its built-in solver. To use any other optimizer:

- `prob.x`, `prob.lower`, `prob.upper`: the current values and the bounds of the knobs
- `value(prob, x)`: the residual vector at the knob values `x`: for each target its weight times
  its distance from its goal (zero where it is met), then `minimize_weight` times each
  expression to minimize
- `SciBmad.value_and_jacobian(prob, x)`: the residuals and their exact Jacobian in the knobs
- `penalty(prob, x)`: the sum of the squared residuals, `Inf` where the lattice has no solution
  (for optimizers that take a scalar and no derivatives, e.g. genetic algorithms)
- `setknobs!(prob, x)`: sets the knobs

These functions leave the knobs at `x`.

The sum of the squared residuals is what is minimized, so targets and expressions to minimize
are balanced against each other when they cannot all vanish. Larger target weights (or a smaller
`minimize_weight`) hold the targets more tightly.

The current values of the expressions ([`LatticeExpr`](@ref)s) `exprs` and their exact derivatives

TrackConfig:
struct TrackConfig

Defines configuration settings for a particles tracking run.

## Properties
- `n_turns::Int`: Number of turns, defaults to `1`
- `save_every_n_turns::Int`: Multiple of turn number which specifies the turns tracking 
    data is saved, defaults to `1`
- `in_body_coordinates::Bool`: If `true`, particles saved inside misaligned elements are not
    transformed back to the reference curve coordinates. Default is `false`
- `save_reference::Bool`: If `true`, the reference time and energy at each location and saved
    turn are saved too (`t_ref` and `beta_gamma_ref` of the result). This compiles the tracking
    separately and makes it slower (the reference time is computed at every integration step).
    Default is `false`
- `scalar_params::Bool`: If `true`, only uses the primal values of any `LatElement` 
    properties set as `GTPSA.TPS`, `ForwardDiff.Dual`, or `ReverseDiff.TrackedReal` 
    (ignores derivatives part, useful for closed orbit finding prior to parametric 
    normal form). Default is `false`
- `rf_on::Bool`: If `false`, then any `RFParams` in any `LatElement`s are ignored for the 
    entirety of the tracking. Default is `true`
- `ramp_particle_energy_without_rf::Bool`: If `true` when ramping (`Beamline`'s reference 
    energy is a `TimeFunction`), then particle energies will be artificially ramped with 
    the reference energy. Default is `false`
- `ramp_update_each_particle::Bool`: If `true` when ramping, then each particle sees the
    reference energy at its own time (from its z-offset) at the element entrances, and the
    reference energy also changes through each element. If `false`, all particles see the
    reference energy at the reference time at each element entrance. Usually only needed if
    ramping is fast compared to the time scale of bunch passage through elements. (Time-dependent
    element parameters are always evaluated at each particle's own time.) Default is `false`.
- `batch_start::Int`: Specifies the starting index for `BatchParam`s that particles in a 
    bunch will see. E.g., if `batch_start=3`, then particle 1 sees index 3 in all 
    `BatchParam`s, particle 2 sees index 4, etc. Indexing of `BatchParam`s will loop 
    around to the start if the particle index exceeds the length of the `BatchParams`. 
    Default is `1`. WARNING: setting this argument will caused unaligned memory access on 
    the GPU, which may reduce performance. In this case, consider `circshift`-ing all 
    `BatchParam`s instead.
- `verbose::Bool`: If `true`, print the the status of tracking. Default is `false`
- `groupsize::Int`: Designates a group of threads acting in parallel, preferably in 
    lockstep. If tracking on a CUDA GPU, this is equal to the "block" size. On the CPU, 
    would be a multiple of the vector register width. Default is `0` which lets 
    `KernelAbstractions` decide.
- `use_cpu_multithreading::Bool `: If `true`, then CPU multithreading will be used. Only 
    beneficial for a large number of particles, as there is a cost to launching threads. 
    Default is `false`.
- `use_KA::Bool`: If `true`, uses `KernelAbstractions` to launch tracking kernels. Default 
    is `true`, and it must be `true` for the GPU. 
- `use_explicit_SIMD::Bool`: If `true`, uses `SciBmad`'s explicit CPU SIMD tracking, which
    often guarantees vectorization of tracking on the CPU. Default is `!use_KA`

The point of the tracking at which the callbacks are executed, passed to each callback as
`callback(i, coords, p::TrackPoint)`. Its properties are:

  position of the `Bunch`: from the beginning of the element for a new `Bunch`)
- `t_ref`: reference time
- `step`: integration steps from the beginning of the `Beamline` (`n_slices*n_steps` per element,
  the last one at the exit of the element; when tracking a single element, continued from the
  position of the `Bunch` as `s`)
- `beta_gamma_ref`: reference energy (beta*gamma)
- `last_ds_step`: length of the last integration step
- `last_g`: curvature `(gx, gy)` of the last integration step

`transforms_out!(i, coords, p)` and `transforms_in!(i, coords, p)` transform particle `i` out of

The transforms are only computed when used.
TrackResult:
struct TrackResult

Contains all information for a given particle tracking run. The particles are read at locations
of the beamline (given as for the columns of `twiss`; without a location, the only saved
location, by default the end of the beamline), for a saved turn and a particle:

```julia
res.x[turn=2]                     # x of all particles after turn 2 (at the only saved location)
res.x[turn=2, particle=1]         # of particle 1
res.x[]                           # [particle, saved turn]
res.px[qd, turn=2]                # at the beginning of the element qd (see `at` in `track`)
res.v[qd, :exit, particle=1]      # all six coordinates at its end: [coordinate, saved turn]
```

## Properties
- `x`, `px`, `y`, `py`, `z`, `pz`: the coordinates, `v`: all six (the coordinate is the second
  index), `q`: the spin quaternions if spin was tracked, `state`: the state of the particles
  (`STATE_ALIVE`, ...), `t_ref`, `beta_gamma_ref`: the reference time and energy (one value per
  location and turn) if `save_reference=true`. See [`TrackColumn`](@ref) for how they are read
- `turns`: the saved turns (turn 0: the initial coordinates; `NaN` at the locations before
  `start`)
- `start`: the beamline index of the element where the tracking started (see `start` in
  [`track`](@ref))
- `s`, `index`, `name`, `kind`: the s, the beamline index (`-1` for the end of the beamline), the
  name and the kind of the element of each saved location
- `data`: the saved arrays, indexed by location number (in the order of `s`) and saved turn (1:
  the initial coordinates): `state[particle, location, saved turn]`,
  `v[particle, coordinate, location, saved turn]`, `q[particle, quaternion, location, saved turn]`
  (or `nothing`), `t_ref[location, saved turn]` and `beta_gamma_ref[location, saved turn]` (or
  `nothing`; per particle with `BatchParam`s: a `BatchParam` for each location and turn)
- `config`: the `TrackConfig`, `elapsed_time`: the tracking time in seconds, `bunch`: the
  `Bunch` at the end of tracking
TwissColumn:
TwissColumn

A column of a `Twiss` table (e.g. `tw.beta1`), indexed with locations of the beamline exactly as
the columns of a [`TwissExpr`](@ref):

- `tw.beta1[qd]`, `tw.beta1[5]`: at the beginning of the element `qd` (one value; `qd` must be
  placed once in the beamline, else it is an error), or of the element with beamline index 5.
  Elements made from `qd` (copies, also of copies) are placements of `qd`
- `tw.beta1[[qd]]`: at the beginning of every placement of `qd`, in beamline order (a vector)
- `tw.beta1[begin]`, `tw.beta1[end]`: at the beginning and the end of the beamline (or of the part
  of it given with `start` and `stop`). As an index, `end` is the beamline index of the end (one
  more than the number of elements, or the index of `stop`), so `tw.beta1[end-1]` is at the
  beginning of the last element
- `tw.beta1[5, :exit]`, `tw.beta1[qd, :exit]`: at the end of the element (the beginning of the
  next one). The end of the beamline is like a zero-length element: `[end]`, `[end, :entrance]`
  and `[end, :exit]` are the same location
- `tw.beta1[5, :]`, `tw.beta1[qd, :]`: at every integration step of the element, both ends
  included (a vector)
- `tw.beta1[5, 2]`, `tw.beta1[qd, 2]`: two integration steps after the beginning of the element
- `tw.beta1["q*"]`, `tw.beta1[r"..."]`, `tw.beta1[[qf, qd]]`, `tw.beta1[2:5]`: at the beginning
  of the elements found by name (as for `findelements`), or of each element given (a vector).
  With a position, e.g. `tw.beta1[[qd], :exit]`, at that position of each
- `tw.beta1[(2.0, 10.0)]`, `tw.beta1[:]`: at every integration step in an s-range (and the end
  of the beamline if the range contains it), or of the whole beamline (a vector)

In the table of a part of the beamline (`start`, `stop`), a vector has the locations in the part
only, an element must be placed once in the part, and a beamline index outside it is an error.
The table must have rows at these locations (it has with the default `at`). The column also
iterates over all rows of the table, in order, and broadcasts (`tw.dbeta1 ./ tw.beta1`) as a vector
of them; `collect(tw.beta1)` (or `tw.df.beta1`) is that vector, and `first` and `last` are its
first and last rows.
TwissExpr:
TwissExpr(bl::Beamline; kwargs...)

The quantities of `twiss(bl; kwargs...)` as expressions ([`LatticeExpr`](@ref)), computed only
when they are needed (by [`value`](@ref), [`SciBmad.value_and_jacobian`](@ref) or [`match!`](@ref)), and
then only at the locations used. `kwargs` are those of `twiss` (`rf_on`, `a_initial`, `spin`,
`delta0`, ...) except `at`, `cols`, `base_cols`, `as_taylor_series` and `GTPSA_descriptor`, which
are set from the expressions. The truncation orders are chosen from the quantities used; `order`
can be given to use a higher one.

`a_initial` may be the `a` of another `TwissExpr`, e.g. `TwissExpr(line; a_initial=tw.a[end])`,
to continue the lattice functions of another beamline. `initial` may be a `Context`, whose variables
can then be knobs, e.g. to match the Twiss parameters at the start of a line:
`ini = Context(beta1=10.0, beta2=10.0)`, `TwissExpr(line; initial=ini)`, `@knob(ini.beta1)`.

## Quantities
- Summary values: `tw.q1`, `tw.q2`, `tw.q3`, `tw.etac`, `tw.alphac`, `tw.qspin`, `tw.damp1`, ...
  A derivative of an amplitude-dependent value is selected as for the result of `twiss`, e.g.
  `tw.q1[delta=2]` (∂²q1/∂δ²) or `tw.q1[J1=1]`; `tw.dq1` and `tw.dq2` are short for the
  chromaticities `tw.q1[delta=1]` and `tw.q2[delta=1]`, `tw.dq1_n` for `tw.q1[delta=n]`.
- Columns: `tw.<column>[location]` for every scalar column of `twiss`, including chromatic
  derivatives (`tw.dbeta1`, `tw.dx_2`) and `tw.h<ijkl>`.

## Locations
The same as for the columns of the result of `twiss` (see [`TwissColumn`](@ref)):
- `tw.beta1[ele]`, `tw.beta1[7]`: the beginning of the element (placed once, else an error), or
  of the element with that beamline index. `tw.beta1[[ele]]`: every placement (a vector).
- `tw.beta1[ele, :exit]`: the end of the element.
- `tw.beta1[ele, :]`: every integration step of the element, both ends included (a vector;
  `tw.beta1[[ele], :]` of every placement).
  `tw.beta1[ele, k]`: after `k` integration steps.
- `tw.beta1[end]`, `tw.beta1[begin]`: the end and the beginning of the beamline (or of the part
  given with `start` and `stop`, which vectors are restricted to). `end` is a beamline index:
  `tw.beta1[end-1]` is the beginning of the last element.
- `tw.beta1["q*"]`, `tw.beta1[r"..."]`: elements by name, as for `findelements` (a vector).
- `tw.beta1[(s1, s2)]`, `tw.beta1[:]`: every integration step in an s-range, or of the whole
  beamline (a vector).

Vectors are elementwise: `tw.beta1["q*"]^2`, `tw.beta1["q*"] <= 30` (one target per element),
with `sum`, `mean`, `maximum`, `minimum` and `norm`.

dynamic_aperture:
dynamic_aperture(ring::Beamline; kwargs...) -> NTuple{2,Matrix{Float64}}

Computes the acceptance of the ring by pushing a polar grid in `x/sig_x` and `y/sig_y` 
space, for each of the provided `deltas`. The beam sizes `sig_x` and `sig_y` are those at the
beginning of the beamline for the given emittances. Returns a tuple of two matrices `x_norm_da`,
`y_norm_da`: `x_norm_da[j, i]`, `y_norm_da[j, i]` is the starting position, in units of
`sig_x` and `sig_y`, of the first particle lost along the `j`-th angle of the grid for
`deltas[i]`; `Inf` if no particle along that angle is lost, and the column `i` is zero if the
particle on the closed orbit itself is lost. `BatchParam`s in the lattice are not supported (an
error: each particle of the grid would see another entry).

## Required Keyword arguments
- `n_r::Int`: Number of radial points of the polar grid, from 0 to the maximum: each angle has
    `n_r - 1` particles, and the closed orbit one for each δ
- `n_theta::Int`: Number of angles to sample on the polar grid (see `theta_lims`)
- `deltas::AbstractArray`: Array of each δ to compute the transverse acceptance
- `max_sig_x::Real`: Maximum sigma-x of the polar grid, in units of sigma (e.g. 
    `max_sig_x=20` to check up to 20 sigma)
- `max_sig_y::Real`: Maximum sigma-y of the polar grid, in units of sigma (e.g. 
    `max_sig_y=20` to check up to 20 sigma)
- `emit_1::Real`: Horizontal-like emittance to assume [m]
- `emit_2::Real`: Vertical-like emittance to assume [m]
- `n_turns::Int`: Number of turns to track

## Optional Keyword Arguments
- `backend`: A CPU/GPU device backend to use, e.g. `CPU()`, or `CUDA.CUDABackend()` to 
    use the GPU. Default is `CPU()`
- `coordinates_number_type::Type`: The type of the phase space coordinates to use in 
    tracking. Default is `Float64`
- `delta_dependent_orbits::Bool`: If `true`, then for each δ in `deltas`, the 
    computed acceptance line will be centered around that δ-dependent closed orbit 
    (computed with `rf_on=false`). Else, all acceptance lines are centered around the 
    6D closed orbit. Default is `true` if coasting beam is detected, `false` if 
    longitudinal motion is detected. The tracking itself includes RF cavities in either case,
    unless `rf_on=false` is given too.
- `theta_lims`: A tuple specifying the range of thetas to scan on the polar grid. Default 
    is `(0, pi)`, the upper half plane (`y >= 0`)
- `sig_pz::Real`: sigma-δ of the beam to assume, default is 0
- `emit_3::Real`: Longitudinal-like emittance to assume [m]
- `output_file`: If provided, then a file containing the initial particle coordinates (w.r.t. 
    the closed orbit(s)) as rows, with the last column specifying the particle state at the 
    end of tracking, will be written to the file. Default is `nothing`.
- `track_kwargs...`: Any of the settings in `TrackConfig` except for `n_turns` and 
    `save_every_n_turns` may be provided to configure the tracking.
find_closed_orbit:
find_closed_orbit(bl::Beamline; v0=zeros(1, 6), kwargs...)

Finds the closed orbit of the beamline `bl` using the initial guess `v0`. Supports batched-
closed orbit finding including `BatchParam`s and/or different δ-dependent closed orbits in 
rings with coasting beam, simply by including more particles in the guess `v0`. 

A named tuple is returned containing the following fields:
- `v0`: The initial matrix `v0`, mutated to contain the result
- `coasting_beam`: `true` if coasting beam, `false` otherwise
- `sol`: Another named tuple containing Newton solver convergence information (see 
    `SciBmad.BatchSolve.newton`), including the Jacobian(s) for the particle(s) at the last 
    iteration.

This function is GPU-parallelizable by specifying `v0` as a `GPUArray` (e.g. `CuArray`), and 
will use CUBLAS's batched linear system solvers for the Newton solve.

## Keyword arguments
- `v0`: Matrix of size `(n_particles, 6)` as the initial guess. If `n_particles > 1`, batched 
    closed orbit finding will be used. **NOTE:** `v0` will be mutated in place with the result!
    Default is `zeros(1, 6)`.
- `reltol`: Relative convergence tolerance of the Newton solver, default is `1e-13`
- `abstol`: Absolute convergence tolerance of the residual norm, default is `1e-13`
- `maxiter`: Maximum iterations for the Newton root finder before failure, default is `100`
- `rf_on::Bool`: If `false`, then any `RFParams` in any `LatElement`s are ignored for the 
    entirety of the tracking. Default is `true`.
- `batch_start::Int`: Specifies the starting index for `BatchParam`s that particles in a 
    bunch will see. E.g., if `batch_start=3`, then particle 1 sees index 3 in all 
    `BatchParam`s, particle 2 sees index 4, etc. Indexing of `BatchParam`s will loop 
    around to the start if the particle index exceeds the length of the `BatchParams`. 
    Default is `1`. WARNING: setting this argument will caused unaligned memory access on 
    the GPU, which may reduce performance. In this case, consider `circshift`-ing all 
    `BatchParam`s instead.
- `autodiff`: Automatic-differentiation backend to use (e.g. `AutoForwardDiff()`, `AutoEnzyme()`, 
    `AutoGTPSA()`, etc.). Default is `AutoForwardDiff`. See `ADTypes.jl` for all supported backends.
- `warn`: If `true`, warnings about the result will be printed. Default is `true`
- `coast_tol`: Tolerance for the first-order delta dependences on each of the phase space variables below 
    which coasting beam is assumed. Default is `1e-14`.
- `coasting_beam`: Bool that can be optionally specified as `true` or `false` to bypass the coasting-
    beam check and save some computation time.
- `batch`: Optionally specify if batched-solution is used as `Val{true}()` or `Val{false}()` to improve 
    type-stability of this function.
- `prep`: A `DifferentiationInterface.JacobianPrep` object to use for the automatic-differentation backend.
    Default is `nothing` meaning to construct one automatically using the `autodiff` backend

## Examples
```julia
qf = Quadrupole(Kn1=0.36, L=0.5)
d = Drift(L=1.2)
qd = Quadrupole(Kn1=-0.36, L=0.5)
kick = HKicker(Kn0L=1e-5)

fodo = Beamline([qf, d, qd, d, kick], 
        species_ref=Species("electron"), E_ref=18e9) # some Beamline
co_sol = find_closed_orbit(fodo)

# To get delta-dependent closed orbits:
v0 = [0. 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.1e-2; # δ = 0.1e-2
      0. 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.2e-2] # δ = 0.2e-2

co_sol = find_closed_orbit(fodo, v0=v0)

# With BatchParams
kick.Kn0L = BatchParam([1e-5, 2e-5])
v0 = zeros(2, 6)
co_sol = find_closed_orbit(fodo, v0=v0)

# BatchParams + delta-dependent closed orbits:
v0 = [0. 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.1e-2; # δ = 0.1e-2
      0. 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.2e-2] # δ = 0.2e-2
co_sol = find_closed_orbit(fodo, v0=v0)
```
findelements:
findelements(where::Union{Lattice,Branch,Beamline}, pattern::Union{AbstractString,Regex}) -> Vector{LatElement}

Returns all the `LatElement`s in `where` that match `pattern`. `where` may be a `Lattice`, a
`Branch`, or a `Beamline`. The returned elements are ordered by the order of the branches
followed by their order in the branch, and each element appears at most once. No match is not an error, and an empty vector is returned.

## Syntax

The syntax is based on Bmad's. An "atom" is of the form
```
  {branch>>}{kind::}name{#N}
```
where `{...}` marks an optional part and
- `branch`   Match only elements in a `Branch` whose name matches.
- `kind`     Match only elements whose `kind` is `kind`, e.g. `Quadrupole`. This must be an exact match.
- `name`     Element name to match, or an integer element index where the first element of a
  `Branch` (or of the `Beamline` when `where` is a `Beamline`) has index 1. With an index and no
  `branch`, the element with that index in each branch searched is matched.
- `#N`       Match only the `N`th element in each branch that matches the rest of the atom.

Atoms may be combined:
```
  atom1:atom2    # Range: All elements from atom1 through atom2 inclusive.
  set1, set2     # Union.
  set1 & set2    # Intersection.
```
`&` has the lowest precedence, so `A, B & C` is the intersection of `A, B` with `C`. A range is
evaluated in each branch where both `atom1` and `atom2` match, and it is an error if either
matches more than one element in that branch. If `atom2` comes before `atom1`, the range wraps
around the end of the branch.

## Name matching

If `pattern` is a `String`, the branch and element names may use the Bmad wild card
characters `*`, which matches any number of characters (including zero), and `%` or `?`, either
of which matches any single character. There are no other wildcard characters here.

If `pattern` is a `Regex`, e.g. `r"q[0-9]+"`, the branch and element names are Julia regular
expressions. Each must match the whole name, so `r"Q"` does not match an element named `Q1`.
The flags of `pattern` (e.g. `i` for case insensitive) are applied to each. Operator characters
in a regex group `(...)`, character class `[...]`, or quantifier `{n,m}`, or that are escaped
with a backslash, are part of the regular expression.

Matching is case sensitive unless the `i` flag is used with a `Regex`.

## Examples
```julia
findelements(lat, "q*")                     # Elements whose name begins with "q".
findelements(lat, r"q.*")                   # Same as above using a regex.
findelements(lat, r"q.*"i)                  # Same as above but case insensitive, so "Q1" also matches.
findelements(lat, "Quadrupole::q%")         # Quadrupoles with a two character name starting with "q".
findelements(lat, "Quadrupole::q?")         # Same as above. "?" and "%" are equivalent.
findelements(lat, "ring>>7")                # 7th element of the branch named "ring".
findelements(lat, "b*>>bpm#2")              # 2nd element named "bpm" in each branch with a name
                                            #   starting with "b".
findelements(lat, "m1:m2")                  # Elements from "m1" through "m2" in a line.
findelements(lat, "Marker::* & m1:m2")      # Markers from "m1" through "m2".
findelements(lat, "q1, q2")                 # Elements named "q1" or "q2".
findelements(lat, r"(q|s)[0-9]{1,2}")       # Regex with operator characters in a group and quantifier.
```

See also `findbranches`.
match!:
match!(; vary, targets=[], minimize=[], kwargs...) -> MatchResult
    match!(bl::Beamline; vary, targets, twiss=(;), kwargs...)
    match!(prob::MatchProblem; kwargs...)
    match!(res::MatchResult; kwargs...)

Varies the [`Knob`](@ref)s `vary` (also `obj => :property` pairs) until the [`Target`](@ref)s
`targets` are met, and leaves the lattice there. `minimize` are expressions whose sum of squares is
made as small as possible together with the distances from the targets (each times its `weight`;
the expressions times `minimize_weight`, default `1`). Targets are written with expressions
([`LatticeExpr`](@ref)) of the quantities of a [`TwissExpr`](@ref):

```julia
tw = TwissExpr(cell)
match!(vary=[@knob(qf.Kn1), @knob(qd.Kn1)], targets=[tw.q1 == 0.25, tw.q2 == 0.25])
```

Given a `Beamline`, `targets` (and `minimize`) may be functions of its `TwissExpr` (made with the
`twiss` keyword arguments in `twiss`), which can also be written as a `do` block:

```julia
match!(cell; vary=[@knob(qf.Kn1), @knob(qd.Kn1)], targets = tw -> [tw.q1 == 0.25, tw.q2 == 0.25])
```

The derivatives are exact (see [`SciBmad.value_and_jacobian`](@ref)). The solver is the
Levenberg-Marquardt method of `BatchSolve` (`BatchSolve.levenberg_marquardt!`): steps that do
not reduce the residuals, or where the lattice has no solution (e.g. it is unstable), are
rejected and shorter ones taken, so there may be fewer, as many, or more targets than knobs.
Knobs stay within their bounds and step limits, and `<=` and `>=` targets only count while they
are violated. Like every such method it finds a nearby solution: targets of very different size
(a tune and a beta function) should get `weight`s that make their residuals comparable. To use
another optimizer, see [`MatchProblem`](@ref).

## Keyword arguments
- `maxiter`: Maximum number of iterations, default is `50`
- `verbose`: If `true`, prints the progress of the solver at each iteration. Default is `false`
- `solver`: `:levenberg_marquardt` (default), or `:gauss_newton`: Gauss-Newton steps from the
    singular value decomposition of the Jacobian (their halves, quarters and eighths, then
    damped steps, where a step does not reduce the residuals)
- `rcond`: For `solver=:gauss_newton`, singular values of the Jacobian below `rcond` times the
    largest are ignored (knob combinations the targets do not respond to). Default is `1e-10`

Returns a [`MatchResult`](@ref). `match!(res)` continues the match from the current lattice.
naff:
naff(data::AbstractMatrix, n_frequencies=1; window_order=1) -> (frequencies, amplitudes)

Performs a batched Numerical Analysis of Fundamental Frequencies (NAFF) method for 
the (complex) signals in each row of `data`, computing the first `n_frequencies`
frequencies from the signal. A Hanning window with order `window_order` is applied 
to the signal in order to gain a more accurate computation of the frequencies.

# Arguments
- `data::AbstractMatrix`: a matrix of size `num_signals x n_samples` to do NAFF on
- `n_frequencies = 1`: number of frequencies to compute with NAFF

# Keyword Arguments
- `window_order = 1`: order of the Hanning window applied to the signal throughout NAFF
- `warnings = true`: display warnings

# Output
- `frequencies`: a matrix of size `num_signals x n_frequencies` containing the frequencies
- `amplitudes`: a matrix of size `num_signals x n_frequencies` containing the complex 
                amplitudes associated with each frequency
phase_trombone!:
phase_trombone!(ele::LatElement; phi1=0, phi2=0, phi3=0)

Makes `ele` into a phase trombone - a matrix expanded around the _current_ closed orbit 
(at the time of calling this function) which applies a linear rotation in normal form 
coordinates (which are also computed at the time of calling this function). Useful for 
creating zero-length elements where the phase advance can be tuned without impacting the 
linear optics. The `LatElement` must be in a `Beamline` in order to 
use this function.

`phi1`, `phi2`, and `phi3` are the changes of the phase advances of the three normal modes, in 
units of 2π (i.e. the changes of the tunes). The `LatElement` property `transport_map` is filled 
with the corresponding phase trombone transport map, and `transport_map_params` with its parameters. 
The first three entries of `transport_map_params` are `phi1`, `phi2`, and `phi3`, and can be 
changed later to change the phase advances.

Spin tracking is NOT currently compatible with phase trombones.
  
!!! warn
    If the closed orbit and/or linear optics at `ele` are changed *after* calling 
    this function, then the phase trombone map is no longer valid.
rawget:
rawget(p::AbstractParams, key::Symbol)
    rawget(ele::LatElement, key::Symbol)

Gets the independent variable `key` of the parameter group `p` or of the element `ele` exactly
as it is stored, without evaluating deferred expressions: e.g. a `DefExpr` set for `Kn1` is
returned as that `DefExpr`. Evaluating it with `deval` in the `Context` of the element's
`Beamline` gives `getproperty(ele, key)`.

Properties which are not independent variables but computed from them (e.g. `Kn1L` or `Bn1`
when `Kn1` was set last, `E_ref` when `p_over_q_ref` was set, `s`) cannot be gotten raw, and
give an error.

## Examples
```jldoctest
julia> qf = Quadrupole(Kn1=DefExpr(c -> c.kq), L=0.5);

julia> bl = Beamline([qf], context=Context(kq=0.36));

julia> d = rawget(qf, :Kn1);

julia> qf.Kn1 = 2*d; # Twice the stored expression, still dependent on kq

julia> bl.context.kq = 0.4;

julia> bl[qf].Kn1
0.8
```
track:
track(bl::Beamline; kwargs...) -> TrackResult

All-encompassing function to track particles through the beamline `bl` using the configured 
settings specified by the keyword arguments `kwargs`.

## Keyword Arguments
- `v0`: A matrix of size `(n_particles, 6)` storing the initial particle phase space coordinates
- `spin`: If `true`, spin tracking will be enabled with identity quaternions as initial quaternions
- `q0`: A matrix of size `(n_particles, 4)` storing the initial particle spin quaternions if spin tracking
- `weight`: Optional vector of length `(n_particles)` specifying macroparticle weights per particle, default 
    is `nothing` corresponding to uniform weights for all particles
- `species`: The species of the particles, default the reference species of the beamline
    (`bl.species_ref`)
- `bunch`: Instead of specifying `v0`, `spin`, `q0`, `weight`, and `species`, an initial `Bunch`
    may be explicitly provided
- `start::Union{Integer,LatElement}`: The element (or its beamline index) at whose beginning the
    tracking starts. Default is `1`
- `at::Union{Nothing,Colon,AbstractVector}`: Where the particles are saved, as in `twiss`: a
    vector of locations, each as one index of a column (see [`TrackColumn`](@ref)): elements
    (at the beginning of each placement), beamline indexes, names (as for `findelements`), and
    s-ranges (tuples: the integrator steps inside them, and the end of the beamline if they
    contain it). `:` is every integrator step and the end of the beamline. An entry that is not
    in the beamline is an error. Default is `nothing`, only the end of the beamline. The
    locations are ordered in s (from the beginning of the beamline).
    The locations before `start` are first reached in the second turn: before (turns 0 and 1)
    they are `NaN` (`state` `STATE_PREBORN`)
- `n_turns::Int`: Number of turns, each ending at the end of the beamline (the first turn
    begins at `start`), defaults to `1`
- `save_every_n_turns::Int`: Multiple of turn number which specifies the turns tracking 
    data is saved, defaults to `1`
- `in_body_coordinates::Bool`: If `true`, particles saved inside misaligned elements are not
    transformed back to the reference curve coordinates. Default is `false`
- `save_reference::Bool`: If `true`, the reference time and energy at each location and saved
    turn are saved too (`t_ref` and `beta_gamma_ref` of the result). This compiles the tracking
    separately and makes it slower (the reference time is computed at every integration step).
    Default is `false`
- `scalar_params::Bool`: If `true`, only uses the primal values of any `LatElement` 
    properties set as `GTPSA.TPS`, `ForwardDiff.Dual`, or `ReverseDiff.TrackedReal` 
    (ignores derivatives part, useful for closed orbit finding prior to parametric 
    normal form). Default is `false`
- `rf_on::Bool`: If `false`, then any `RFParams` in any `LatElement`s are ignored for the 
    entirety of the tracking. Default is `true`
- `ramp_particle_energy_without_rf::Bool`: If `true` when ramping (`Beamline`'s reference 
    energy is a `TimeFunction`), then particle energies will be artificially ramped with 
    the reference energy. Default is `false`
- `ramp_update_each_particle::Bool`: If `true` when ramping, then each particle sees the
    reference energy at its own time (from its z-offset) at the element entrances, and the
    reference energy also changes through each element. If `false`, all particles see the
    reference energy at the reference time at each element entrance. Usually only needed if
    ramping is fast compared to the time scale of bunch passage through elements. (Time-dependent
    element parameters are always evaluated at each particle's own time.) Default is `false`.
- `batch_start::Int`: Specifies the starting index for `BatchParam`s that particles in a 
    bunch will see. E.g., if `batch_start=3`, then particle 1 sees index 3 in all 
    `BatchParam`s, particle 2 sees index 4, etc. Indexing of `BatchParam`s will loop 
    around to the start if the particle index exceeds the length of the `BatchParams`. 
    Default is `1`. WARNING: setting this argument will caused unaligned memory access on 
    the GPU, which may reduce performance. In this case, consider `circshift`-ing all 
    `BatchParam`s instead.
- `verbose::Bool`: If `true`, print the the status of tracking. Default is `false`
- `groupsize::Int`: Designates a group of threads acting in parallel, preferably in 
    lockstep. If tracking on a CUDA GPU, this is equal to the "block" size. On the CPU, 
    would be a multiple of the vector register width. Default is `0` which lets 
    `KernelAbstractions` decide.
- `use_cpu_multithreading::Bool `: If `true`, then CPU multithreading will be used. Only 
    beneficial for a large number of particles, as there is a cost to launching threads. 
    Default is `false`.
- `use_KA::Bool`: If `true`, uses `KernelAbstractions` to launch tracking kernels. Default 
    is `true` if `v0` is a GPU array, else `false`.
- `use_explicit_SIMD::Bool`: If `true`, uses `SciBmad`'s explicit CPU SIMD tracking, which
    often guarantees vectorization of tracking on the CPU. Default is `!use_KA`
- `config`: Instead of specifying `n_turns`, `save_every_n_turns`, `in_body_coordinates`,
    `save_reference`, `scalar_params`,
    `ramp_particle_energy_without_rf`, `ramp_update_each_particle`, `verbose`, `groupsize`, 
    `use_cpu_multithreading`, `use_KA`, and `use_explicit_SIMD`, a single `TrackConfig` 
    struct can be provided instead. Setting any of these keyword arguments will override 
    that in `config`.
twiss:
twiss(bl::Beamline; kwargs...)

General function to compute the (parametric and nonlinear) optics of a `Beamline`. 
Returns a `Twiss` struct that contains the (amplitude-dependent) (spin) tunes/slip, and a 
dataframe of the lattice functions at each specified integration step. By default, lattice 
functions of the Sagan-Rubin/Edwards-Teng coupling formalism are computed in the dataframe 
at every integration step. The columns are read at locations of the beamline, e.g. 
`tw.beta1[qd]` at the beginning of the element `qd` (see [`TwissColumn`](@ref)), and the 
whole table is `tw.df`.

The `cols` keyword argument can be set to customize what quantities will be computed and 
stored as columns in the returned dataframe. E.g., 
```julia
tw = twiss(bl; cols=["beta1"])
```
will compute only the horizontal-like beta function. We can also specify so-called 
"resonance driving terms"/"detune coefficients" of the nonlinear effective Hamiltonian,
```julia
tw = twiss(bl; cols=["beta1", "h3000"], order=2)
```
where the total order of the `twiss` call has also been set appropriately to compute `h3000` 
(without `order` and `chrom`, the orders that the columns need are chosen).

An arbitrary order chromatic derivative of any scalar-valued column can be taken using the 
syntax `d<column>_<order>`. If `order==1`, then the `_1` can be omitted. E.g., the linear and 
2nd order dispersions, as well as ∂β₁/∂δ can be computed with
```julia
tw = twiss(bl; cols=["dx", "dx_2","dbeta1"], chrom=2)
```
where the `chrom` keyword argument, which specifies solely the truncation order of δ, has been 
set appropriately. 

Chromatic derivatives need a beam without synchrotron motion: `rf_on=false` if there are RF
cavities.

To customize the output, such as computing higher order (chromatic) lattice functions, spin 
lattice functions/tune, amplitude-dependent tunes, and parametric quantities, see the 
keyword arguments:

## Keyword arguments
- `at::Union{Colon, AbstractVector}`: Where to compute the lattice functions (the rows of the
    table): a vector of locations, each as one index of a column (see [`TwissColumn`](@ref)):
    elements (at the beginning of each placement), beamline indexes, names (as for
    `findelements`), and s-ranges (tuples). Default `:`, every integration step and the end of
    the beamline. An entry that is not in the beamline is an error; in a part of the beamline
    (`start`, `stop`) only the locations in the part are computed.
- `start`, `stop`: Elements (or their beamline indexes) to compute the optics of only
    a part of the beamline: from the beginning of `start` (default: the first element) to the
    beginning of `stop` (default: the end of the beamline). Without `initial` or `a_initial`
    these are the periodic optics of that part by itself (e.g. of one cell of a ring),
    with them those of an open line that starts at `start`. `s` and `index` in the table are
    those of the whole beamline, phases are counted from `start`, and the last row is the
    beginning of `stop`.
- `in_body_coordinates::Bool`: If `true` the lattice functions inside misaligned elements are not
    transformed back to the reference curve coordinates. Default is `false`
- `rf_on::Bool`: If `false`, then any `RFParams` in any `LatElement`s are ignored for the 
    entirety of the Twiss tracking and calculation. Default is `true`
- `order::Integer`: TPSA truncation order for all phase space coordinates used in the Twiss 
    calculation. If neither `order` nor `chrom` is given, both are chosen from `cols` (as 
    [`TwissExpr`](@ref) does): 1 for the default columns, higher for chromatic derivatives 
    (`chrom`) and resonance driving terms (`order`). Default is 1 if only `chrom` is given
- `chrom::Integer`: TPSA truncation order for only δ, default is `order` if `order` is given
- `GTPSA_descriptor::Union{Descriptor,Nothing}`: Custom GTPSA `Descriptor` to use for the Twiss 
    calculation, required to provide to do parametric normal form and lattice function 
    calculations. Default is `Descriptor([order, order, order, order, order, chrom], max(order,chrom))`.
- `initial`: The lattice functions at the start of an "open" line (e.g. a transfer line), by name:
    `beta1`, `beta2` (required), `alpha1`, `alpha2`, the coupling `c11`, `c12`, `c21`, `c22`, the
    dispersion `dx`, `dpx`, `dy`, `dpy`, and the orbit `x`, `px`, `y`, `py`, `z`, `pz` (all 0 if
    not given; `pz` is δ, else `delta0`), with the meanings of the columns of the same names.
    A `NamedTuple`, a `Dict` (with `Symbol` or `String` keys), a `Context` (whose variables can
    then be knobs of a match), or a row of another table (`tw.df[end, :]`; its other columns are
    ignored). The values may be Taylor series in GTPSA parameters, not in the phase space
    variables or δ. The beam has no synchrotron motion: RF cavities with voltage need
    `rf_on=false` (or a 6D `a_initial`).
    Default is `nothing`, to compute the periodic ("closed") lattice functions
- `a_initial::Union{DAMap,Nothing}`: A `DAMap` of the initial transformation from normal form 
    coordinates to laboratory coordinates, to compute the lattice functions of an "open" line
    (instead of `initial`). A coasting `a_initial` (without synchrotron motion) also needs
    `rf_on=false` if the line has RF cavities with voltage. Default is `nothing`
- `damping::Union{Bool,Nothing}`: Specifies if radiation damping is included. Default is `nothing`,
    which will auto-detect from `a_initial` or the periodic `a`.
- `delta0`: If the beam is coasting (no longitudinal oscillations), then the optics will 
    be computed around this delta-dependent orbit. Else, this will be an initial guess for the 
    6D closed orbit calculation. Default is `0.`. If `a_initial` is provided then this will be ignored, 
    UNLESS `a_initial` is coasting, in which case this will set the value for δ. With `initial`, it
    is δ if `initial` has no `pz`.
- `v0`: Initial guess for the closed orbit finder if `a_initial` is not provided, else setting this 
    will override the orbit expansion origin coordinates in `a_initial.v0`. Not with `initial`,
    which gives the orbit.
- `spin::Bool`: If `true`, spin is included in the Twiss calculation. Default is `false`, or `true` if 
    `a_initial` includes spin.
- `base_cols`: A vector of "base columns", that will always be included in the Twiss dataframe regardless 
    of what is specified in `cols`. Defaults to the global variable `SciBmad.base_cols`, which defaults 
    to `["index", "name", "kind", "s"]`.
- `cols`: A vector of columns to include in the Twiss dataframe. See the extended help for all possible 
    columns.
- `as_taylor_series::Union{Bool,Nothing}`: If `true`, the lattice functions in the dataframe are 
    returned as Taylor series types - this will be necessary if doing parametric normal form. Default 
    is `nothing`, which autoselects to `false` if there are no parameters in the GTPSA, and `true` if 
    there are parameters.
- `coast_tol`: Tolerance for the first-order delta dependences on each of the phase space variables below 
    which coasting beam is assumed, passed to `find_closed_orbit`. Default is `1e-14`.
- `symplectic_tol::Float64`: Tolerance of symplectic condition violation, above which radiation damping 
    is assumed. Default is `1e-8`.
- `batch_index::Int`: If any element parameters are `BatchParam`, sets which index in the batch the `twiss`
    should be evaluated at. Default is `1`. Batched element lengths and a batched reference
    energy are not supported in `twiss` yet.

To see a description of all quantities available to include in `cols`, see the extended help 
section using `??twiss`

# Extended help

Columns to include in `cols` are detailed below. As a reminder, an arbitrary order chromatic derivative 
of *any* scalar-valued output can be computed using the syntax "d<column>_<order>" (e.g. "dx_1" is the 
linear dispersion).

- `index`  : Beamline index of the containing `LatElement`
- `name`   : Name of the containing `LatElement`
- `kind`   : Kind of the containing `LatElement`
- `s`      : s-position of the row (may be inside of `LatElement`)
- `beta1`  : Horizontal-like beta function of the Sagan-Rubin/Edwards-Teng coupling formalism
- `beta2`  : Vertical-like beta function of the Sagan-Rubin/Edwards-Teng coupling formalism
- `alpha1` : Horizontal-like alpha function of the Sagan-Rubin/Edwards-Teng coupling formalism
- `alpha2` : Vertical-like alpha function of the Sagan-Rubin/Edwards-Teng coupling formalism
- `phi1`   : Horizontal-like phase advance in units of [2π]
- `phi2`   : Vertical-like phase advance in units of [2π]
- `phi3`   : Longitudinal-like phase advance in units of [2π]
- `dampdec1`: Horizontal-like damping decrement
- `dampdec2`: Vertical-like damping decrement
- `dampdec3`: Longitudinal-like damping decrement
- `slip`   : Derivative of z/β₀ with δ from the start of the table: -c times the change of the

- `x`      : Orbit canonical x coordinate
- `px`     : Orbit canonical px coordinate
- `y`      : Orbit canonical y coordinate
- `py`     : Orbit canonical py coordinate
- `z`      : Orbit canonical z coordinate
- `pz`     : Orbit canonical pz coordinate

withvalues:
withvalues(f, c::Context; name=value, ...)

Calls `f()` with the variables of `c` set to the given values, and restores them afterwards, also
if `f` throws (as `push!` and `pop!`). Returns what `f` returns.

## Examples
```julia
withvalues(ring.context; vrf = 0.0) do
  twiss(ring)
end
```
